findings.claim: A 2xx health response with a JSON body of `{ "status": "error" }` is reported as unhealthy, violating the requirement to treat any 2xx response as healthy.
findings.evidence: Acceptance criterion `Runtime health polling`: "treat any 2xx response (including an empty body) as healthy"; hunk `pingEndpoint` parses a 2xx body and returns `{ status: (json.status as "ok" | "error") ?? "ok" }`, so a 200 body with `status: "error"` becomes an error.
findings.suggested_fix: For any `res.ok`, return `{ status: "ok" }` regardless of response body, or ignore `json.status` for health reachability.

findings.claim: `isPending` is delegated to the underlying single mutation state and is not tracked per overlapping call, so it can stop representing whether any mutation is still in flight.
findings.evidence: The adapter adds per-call tokens for results in `calls.current`, but it never tracks an in-flight count; it returns `const { isPending, isSuccess, isError } = entityMutation.state` directly while supporting overlapping calls in `mutateAsync`.
findings.suggested_fix: Maintain an adapter-level pending counter/set keyed by token and expose `isPending` as `pendingCount > 0`.
